lead: Virginia faces tidal flooding in Hampton Roads, mountain floods and winter storms. DryFlare helps owners from Virginia Beach to Richmond and Roanoke dry out fast.
risk: tidal and storm flooding on the coast, mountain flash floods and winter storms
why: Hampton Roads has some of the fastest rising seas on the East Coast. Norfolk and Virginia Beach streets flood at high tide many times a year, and storms make it worse. Hurricane Isabel in 2003 pushed surge into homes from the Chesapeake to Richmond.

The mountains face sudden floods. Helene destroyed much of Damascus in southwest Virginia in 2024. Camille's rain in 1969 is still the benchmark in Nelson County. Winter storms bring ice dams and frozen pipes in Northern Virginia and the Shenandoah. Maryland and North Carolina share many of these storms.
image_alt: Street flooding near homes after heavy rain and high tide
image_caption: Tidal flooding in Norfolk and Virginia Beach can reach homes even without a big storm.
problems: Southwest Virginia and the Blue Ridge
tips: Check tide forecasts in Hampton Roads before big storms.
Seal and dehumidify your crawl space.
Insulate pipes in outside walls before winter.
Buy flood insurance even outside high-risk zones.
insurance: Virginia homeowners policies do not cover tidal or surge flooding, so coastal owners need a separate flood policy.

faq.q: Does homeowners insurance cover tidal flooding in Norfolk?
faq.a: No. Tidal and surge flooding count as flood, which needs a separate NFIP or private policy. Leaks from a burst pipe or a storm-damaged roof are usually covered by homeowners insurance.

licensing_faq: Yes. The Virginia Board for Contractors licenses contractors for most jobs. Plumbing and electrical work need licensed tradespeople.
